title: High-Level Waste Glass – Waste Treatment Completion Company
tools: Software Engineering (Python, PyQt) · Data Analysis (Processing Pipelines)
blurb: Led the student team building a Python desktop app for safety-critical calculations in Hanford radioactive-waste vitrification: glass recipes for tank waste, and each canister's chemical and radiological inventory.
long: The Hanford Site in Washington stores about 56 million gallons of radioactive waste in 177 underground tanks. The plan is vitrification: melting the waste into glass for safe long-term storage. Each batch needs a glass recipe, and each canister needs a record of what went into it.

Our client's preliminary code did those calculations. As lead technical developer I turned it into a Python application with data-analysis pipelines built for auditability, consistency and maintainability: the user picks a melter train and campaign, runs the five processing steps, and every run is archived with its inputs for traceability.
I documented the implementation, wrote the developer handover document, and managed the student team through task delegation and conflict resolution.
highlights: Safety-critical calculations with traceable, archived runs
Five-step processing workflow in a desktop app
Led the team and wrote the developer handover
